headline: Indigenous-Led Fund Transforms Conservation by Trusting Local Communities
meta_description: The Home Planet Fund gives unrestricted funding directly to Indigenous and local communities leading conservation efforts in four critical ecosystems worldwide.
summary_short: An Indigenous-led nonprofit is reshaping conservation funding by giving unrestricted money directly to local communities working to protect the planet's most critical ec…
body:
The Home Planet Fund, founded by Dilafruz Khonikboyeva, is proving that conservation works best when communities closest to the land make the decisions. Rather than imposing rigid timelines and spending requirements, the organization provides unrestricted funding to Indigenous and local communities already engaged in environmental protection across four critical ecosystems: the Tongass Rainforest of Alaska, the glaciers of Central and South Asia known as "the third pole," the grasslands of East Africa, and the South Pacific. By trusting communities to adapt their work to real conditions on the ground, the fund challenges a sector accustomed to spreadsheets and predetermined outcomes.

Khonikboyeva, who grew up in Soviet-occupied Tajikistan, brings hard-won understanding to her work. She rejects what she calls the false narrative that unrestricted giving means handing over money and disappearing. Instead, it means "sitting in enough trust" so communities can return and say plans must shift—not because of failure, but because circumstances changed. This approach recognizes that environmental work, like life itself, doesn't follow neat three-month metrics. The fund deliberately includes elders, youth groups, women's groups, and whole communities in decision-making, ensuring durability beyond the funding period.

Beyond the environmental goal lies something deeper: healing. Khonikboyeva speaks of healing both land and the people who tend it. Having witnessed communities endure extraordinary hardship while maintaining profound bonds of mutual care, she believes this healing work is inseparable from conservation itself. The philosophy is simple but radical in the philanthropic world—invest in what local people already know works, let them continue learning and growing, and recognize that in healing the earth, something in humanity also mends.
quick_facts: Indigenous-led fund provides unrestricted money to local conservation communities
Works across four critical ecosystems: Alaska rainforest, Central Asian glaciers, East African grasslands, South Pacific
Founded by Dilafruz Khonikboyeva, who grew up in Soviet-occupied Tajikistan
Emphasizes trust-based funding that adapts to real conditions, not rigid timelines
